title: Hierarchical reservation annex and spread provisioner
author: Priya Menon
description:
Motivation: long-running customer workloads on Dedicated show imbalanced consumption across GPU pools when tenants request fractional reservations and burst capacity. Existing reservation allocator favours first-fit allocation and causes hot pools and cold pools. This PR introduces a Hierarchical Reservation Annex (HRA) and a Spread Provisioner to improve cross-pool fairness, reduce long-tail latency regressions during bursts, and make headroom estimation more robust for tiered commitments.

Design summary: the HRA is a lightweight policy layer that maintains per-tenant reservation sub-entries (annexes) that can be either leaf (pinned to a pool) or floating (eligible across a spread set). The Spread Provisioner performs a probabilistic spread placement: when committing a reservation it picks a primary pool and 2 auxiliary pools based on inverse-utilization scoring and affinity, then records a compact allowance bitmap used by the runtime to route transient bursts. This enables soft-migration of in-flight burst work without heavyweight reallocation.

Key behaviors: 1) Reservation splitting: large tenant reservations can be split into n annex entries (configurable per-tenant) with proportional capacity fractions. 2) Spread probing window: new reservations can opt into a probe mode for the first 10 minutes to sample cross-pool latency/throughput and refine spread weights. 3) Soft-fallback routing: when primary pool utilization exceeds threshold the runtime will accept routed requests to auxiliary pools up to the annex allowance, with accounting debit applied to the tenant's spread ledger. 4) Telemetry: emits annex_assignment, annex_probe_result, and annex_eviction signals; spreads include per-pool candidate score to support downstream dashboards and alerts.

Compatibility & safety: default behaviour is conservative (annexes disabled) and must be explicitly enabled per-reservation class. All routing decisions are bounded by existing per-tenant concurrency limits and burst budgets; no additional preemption hooks are introduced by this change.

Checklist:
- [x] Planner: annex metadata schema and lease lifecycle
- [x] Provisioner: spread selection algorithm and probe window
- [x] Runtime: read-only annex lookup and soft-route enforcement
- [x] Telemetry: events and metrics for annex lifecycle and probe outcomes
- [x] E2E smoke tests against local simulator and a small Dedicated cluster

Why this is different: instead of global rebalancers or heavier eviction semantics, this approach trades a small amount of reservation bookkeeping for much lower tail latency during bursts by opportunistically accepting traffic on candidate pools and amortizing correctness via spread ledgers. It specifically targets workloads with elastic bursts (short sequence generations, interactive chat) that were suffering from single-pool saturation.

Related: ENG-4921 (tenant imbalance case study), ENG-4978 (reservations telemetry backlog).

review_comments:
Evan Cho (review): Can we bound the size of the annex table growth? Suggest we add a GC pass keyed off last-probe-time and a max-annex-per-tenant cap.
Author (Priya): added max_annex_per_tenant config and a background scavenger that removes tombstoned annexes older than 24h.

Marisol García (review): The spread selection uses inverse-utilization but doesn't consider transient spikes from burst windows; could cause ping-ponging.
Author: implemented a short-term EWMA smoothing on utilization and added a minimum residency time for an annex candidate to avoid flip-flop.

Liam O'Reilly (review): Telemetry looks good, but need to tag probe_result with commit_id and tenant_tier for easier dashboarding.
Author: probe_result now includes commit_id and tenant_tier fields; updated proto and dashboard filters.
merge_outcome: Merged to main after 2 approvals and CI green. Squash merge created single commit 'hierarchical-reservation-annex: add spread provisioner and runtime hooks'
release_notes: Adds Hierarchical Reservation Annex (HRA) and Spread Provisioner: opt-in reservation spreading for better cross-pool fairness during bursts; telemetry for annex lifecycle; config knobs: max_annex_per_tenant, annex_probe_window, annex_aux_candidates. Not enabled by default.
